title: A w-local refinement over the closed points

proof.text: Put $C=B^w$ using [def-weil-pbc-w-localization]. By [lem-weil-pbc-w-localization-points], every point of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ has the form $(x,y)$ with $y\subseteq x$ prime ideals of $B$, contracts to $y$, and has local ring canonically $B_y$. Its closed points are $t_x=(x,x)$ and form a closed subset. The map $B\to C$ is ind-Zariski by its defining presentation.

By the definition of w-locality in [det-pe-wlocal-strict-contractible], the maximal ideals of $R$ form a closed subset $V(I)$; choose any ideal cutting it out. Set $T=(\operatorname{Spec}C)^c\cap V(IC)$. Both factors are closed, so $T$ is Zariski closed and consists of closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Since $t_x$ contracts to $x$ in $B$, it belongs to $V(IC)$ exactly when $I\subseteq x\cap R$. The contraction $x\cap R$ is prime, so this is equivalent to $x\cap R\in V(I)$, hence to $x\cap R$ being maximal. Thus $T=\{t_x:x\cap R\text{ is maximal}\}$.

Apply [def-weil-pbc-retained-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization] with the ring $C$ and the closed subset $T$, and put $B'=C_{[T]}$. The map $C\to B'$ is ind-Zariski. Its points are pairs $(t,q)$ of primes of $C$ with $t\in T$ and $q\subseteq t$, and their local rings are canonically $C_q$. Because every point of $T$ is closed, the lemma makes $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ w-local, with closed points $(t,t)$ indexed by $t\in T$. This proves clause 2.

proof.text: For a point $(t,q)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B'$, write the point $q$ of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ as $(x,y)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-w-localization-points]. The canonical maps identify $B_y\cong C_q\cong B'_{(t,q)}$, the second identification being [lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization]. Their composite is the map induced by $B\to C\to B'$, since each map is the canonical localized structural map. In particular its contraction to $B$ is $y$, and every local ring of $B'$ is the corresponding local ring of $B$, as required in clause 4. A closed point of $B'$ is $(t_x,t_x)$ for $t_x\in T$; its contraction to $R$ is $x\cap R$, which is maximal by step 2. This proves the first assertion of clause 3.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3, local rings and images of closed points

proof.text: The two maps $B\to C$ and $C\to B'$ are ind-Zariski by [def-weil-pbc-w-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization]. Their composite $B\to B'$ is ind-Zariski by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. An ind-Zariski presentation is in particular an ind-étale presentation, by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Applying the composition assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] to the hypothesized ind-étale map $R\to B$ and this ind-étale map $B\to B'$ proves clause 1.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3, composition of algebra maps

proof.text: For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, faithful flatness of $R\to B$ and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] give a prime $x$ of $B$ with $x\cap R=\mathfrak m$. By step 2, $t_x=(x,x)$ belongs to $T$; the closed point $(t_x,t_x)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ supplied in step 3 therefore contracts to $\mathfrak m$. This proves surjectivity on closed points, completing clause 3. If $R$ is the zero ring there are no maximal ideals, so the same argument asserts the required vacuous surjectivity; the constructions permit empty spectra.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3, final sentence (Stacks Tag 00HQ, lemma-ff-rings)
